title: Stardust Power Reports Q3 2026 Financial Results and Business Update
summary: Stardust Power Inc. announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on its corporate...
body_markdown:
**GREENWICH, Conn. – November 13, 2026** – Stardust Power Inc. (“Stardust Power” or the “Company”), an American developer of battery-grade lithium carbonate, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on its corporate developments and the development of its proposed lithium refinery project in Muskogee, Oklahoma.


**Third Quarter 2026 Business Updates and Subsequent Events:**


- **Muskogee Lithium Refinery:** The Company continued to test soil core samples taken from its Muskogee, Oklahoma site as part of the Company’s third-party geotechnical evaluation of site conditions. The proposed refinery project is designed for a nameplate capacity of up to 50,000 mtpa of battery grade lithium carbonate.
- **Houston Office Expansion:** In October 2026, Stardust Power announced the opening of a new office in Houston, Texas, to support project execution, engineering coordination and commercial activities associated with its proposed Muskogee lithium refinery. The Company’s Oklahoma City office remains operational.
- **Conversion of Outstanding Principal Debt:** During the third quarter and subsequent to quarter-end, the Company has no principal balance remaining under the previously disclosed convertible note after converting the outstanding principal into common stock, with approximately $53,000 in accrued default interest remaining payable.
- **Nasdaq Delisting:** Effective October 23, 2026, the Company’s common stock and public warrants were suspended from trading on Nasdaq for the failure to maintain a minimum trading price of $0.10 per share. Management continues to evaluate the Company’s strategic and capital markets alternatives and will provide further updates as appropriate.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights:**


- As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash of approximately $4.6 million, compared to $3.5 million as of December 31, 2025. The increase primarily reflects proceeds from equity financing activities, partially offset by cash used in operations and continued investment in the Muskogee lithium refinery project.
- For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $2.8 million, compared to $4.5 million for the corresponding period in 2025. The decrease primarily reflects lower general and administrative expenses and a favorable change in the fair value of warrant liabilities, partially offset by increased financing-related costs associated with the Company’s capital structure.
- Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.15) for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $(0.53) in the prior-year period. The decrease reflects a lower net loss and a higher weighted average number of common shares outstanding following equity issuances.
- Net cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $6.3 million, compared to $6.5 million during the same period in 2025, reflecting continued investment in advancing the business while maintaining disciplined cash management.
- Net cash used in investing activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $0.3 million, compared to $3.0 million during the same period in 2025, primarily reflecting continued but more measured capital project expenditures related to the development of the Muskogee lithium refinery.
- Net cash provided by financing activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $7.7 million, compared to $10.2 million during the same period in 2025. Financing activities in 2026 primarily reflected proceeds from the Company’s equity financing facilities, while the prior-year period benefited from public offerings and warrant exercises.


### About Stardust Power Inc.


Stardust Power is building one of America’s largest battery-grade lithium carbonate refineries in Muskogee, Oklahoma, strategically located in the center of the United States’ growing energy and manufacturing corridor. The refinery is expected to have production capacity of up to 50,000 metric tons per annum and addresses the critical shortage of U.S. lithium refining capacity. Stardust Power is focused on building a resilient American battery supply chain.
